newsitem.title: USA: Fresenius/North America says consent decree lifted.
newsitem.headline: Fresenius/North America says consent decree lifted.

text.p: Fresenius Medical Care-North America said Tuesday a federal judge had dissolved a consent decree affecting the company, allowing it to proceed with manufacturing operations free of the extraordinary oversight imposed by the decree.
U.S. District Judge Alfred Wolin entered an order January 31 dissolving the 1994 decree between the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and National Medical Care Inc, Fresenius said.
National Medical Care was combined with Fresenius's Dialysis Division in October 1996.
Fresenius said Wolin also dismissed the underlying suit brought by the government, bringing the matter to final resolution.

Fresenius Medical Care-North America, a division of the German-based Fresenius Medical Care A.G., said the court was satisfied, following many comprehensive FDA inspections, that the company had achieved reliable compliance with applicable good manufacturing practice regulations in all facilities subject to the decree.

"The lifting of the 1994 decree allows Fresenius Medical Care-North America to proceed with manufacturing operations free of the extraordinary level of oversight previously imposed by the decree," it said.

National Medical Care voluntarily entered into the decree in January 1994, it said. The decree was comprised of certain obligations and commitments, plus significant potential sanctions for non-compliance.

Fresenius Medical Care-North America manufactures and distributes dialysis products, provides dialysis treatment, performs diagnostic testing, offers homecare services, and conducts laboratory testing.
